Cyber Attack Disrupts Saudi Steel Industry Operations

Dammam – A cyber attack targeting major steel firms in Saudi Arabia has disrupted production and business operations, with Saudi Steel Pipe Co among those affected. The incident, described by industry experts as a ransomware attack, began late Tuesday night and is ongoing as of Wednesday afternoon.

According to company officials, affected firms have temporarily shut down parts of their IT infrastructure, including email servers and production management systems, to contain the breach. “We are working closely with cybersecurity experts and authorities to assess the extent of the attack and restore our systems,” a spokesperson for Saudi Steel Pipe Co said. “Our priority is to protect sensitive data and resume normal operations as quickly as possible.”

Local analysts say the disruption could cause delays in the delivery of steel products to clients across the Kingdom, impacting construction and infrastructure schedules. “The steel industry is a backbone for many ongoing projects in the region, and any prolonged disruption can have a ripple effect,” commented Fahad Al-Qahtani, a Dammam-based industry analyst.

The Saudi Steel Federation issued a statement urging all member firms to implement heightened security measures and back up critical data. “This incident highlights the growing threat of cyber attacks on industrial infrastructure,” the statement read.

At this stage, there is no official estimate of the financial impact, but company sources indicated that several shipments have been delayed and some factory operations remain offline. Investigations into the source and scope of the attack are ongoing.
